headline: Six Years Winless, Yet Unstoppable: Nova Scotia Baseball Team Plays for Pure Joy
meta_description: The Dartmouth High School Spartans haven't won a game in 6 years, yet their enthusiasm remains unshaken. For these Nova Scotia players, it's always been about…
summary_short: Despite six winless seasons and frequent mercy-rule defeats, the Dartmouth High School Spartans from Nova Scotia keep showing up with pure joy and enthusiasm for basebal…
body:
The Dartmouth High School Spartans of Nova Scotia haven't won a baseball game in six years. Yet their enthusiasm remains as strong as ever, with team members showing up season after season simply for the chance to lace up their cleats, pull on their jersey, and play the sport they love. According to team captain Curtis Snelgrove, roughly 80 percent of their losses come via the mercy rule—when a team gives up 10 runs within a certain number of innings. Despite these lopsided defeats, Snelgrove told CBC News that "everyone has a blast on the team, we have a great time." The secret, it turns out, lies in who gets to join. With no performance standards required to make the roster, many young men who've never played baseball before see an opportunity they can't pass up.

One team member, Alex Ansems, exemplified this spirit. Having never played baseball before joining the Spartans, he focused on being what he calls a "vibes guy"—keeping team morale high through sheer enthusiasm and support. That infectious energy has sustained the team through six consecutive winless seasons. Notably, when the Spartans were originally a co-ed team, the female players eventually broke off and formed their own team in the women's league. Shortly after, that team won the first-ever baseball game for the high school. Rather than feeling defeated, the boys celebrated the achievement. "It was pretty awesome to see that Spartans baseball won a game, even if it wasn't my team," said team member Benjamin Boehner. The lesson isn't lost on these young athletes: losing is part of life, and showing up anyway—with optimism and friendship—is what truly matters.
quick_facts: Dartmouth High School Spartans haven't won in 6 years
About 80% of losses decided by mercy rule
Open roster with no performance standards required
Nova Scotia team plays purely for love of the game
Female players broke off, won first game for school
